question: What is the significance of CPM in the context of ad prioritization for video placements?
reference: CPM, or cost per mille, is the bid value of the takeover or sponsored post and is used to order competing ads in the ad prioritization logic for video feed placements. It directly influences how ads are prioritized and displayed within the paginated view of videos.
reference_contexts: Ad Prioritisation Logic for Video Feed Placements Monetize Product | Last updated: April 2026 1. Overview Video feeds on a placement are served in paginated calls of 10 videos each. Two managed ad types can be configured on a placement: Sponsored Takeovers and Sponsored Posts. Each ad is configurable with a CPM, a duration, and a number of creative videos. The system determines what appears in each page of 10 videos based on the priority rules below. This document also defines how the placement-level configuration “Allow content to play with sponsored takeover” changes takeover behaviour. When this setting is disabled for a sponsor, a takeover is composed entirely of the sponsor’s creative videos with no organic content interleaved — the takeover videos cycle to fill all 10 slots per page. Section 10 discusses a planned follow-up: user-level frequency caps, which will diversify the user experience when a sponsored post’s videos would otherwise repeat on the same page for the same user. 2. Placement Configuration The following configurations are set on a placement and directly influence the prioritisation logic: CPM — the bid value of the takeover or sponsored post. Used to order competing ads. Duration — the flight window within which the ad is eligible to serve. Number of creative videos — the set of videos the sponsor has supplied for the ad. In-feed ad slots per page — how many of the 10 slots in a paginated view are reserved for in-feed ads (applies to sponsored posts only). Allow content to play with sponsored takeover (new) — a sponsor-level flag on each takeover. Controls whether organic content can fill the slots not occupied by takeover creative videos on a takeover page. “Allow content to play with sponsored takeover” — behaviour Enabled (default): the takeover fills as many slots as it has creative videos; any remaining slots on that page are filled with organic content. Disabled: the takeover fills as many of the 10 slots as it has creative videos; any remaining slots are empty. Takeovers demand a minimum of 5 videos. This means that with this setting, the backend can send anywhere between 5-10 videos of a takeover to frontend This setting applies only to Sponsored Takeovers. It has no effect on Sponsored Posts or Programmatic ads. 3. Ad Types 3.1 Sponsored Takeover A takeover occupies the entire paginated view. When active, it is the exclusive ad type for that page — no sponsored posts, programmatic ads, or other takeovers can appear alongside it. How the 10 slots on a takeover page are filled depends on the “Allow content to play with sponsored takeover” setting: Enabled: the takeover fills as many of the 10 slots as it has creative videos; any remaining slots are filled with organic content. Disabled: the takeover fills as many of the 10 slots as it has creative videos; any remaining slots are empty. Takeovers demand a minimum of 5 videos. This means that with this setting, the backend can send anywhere between 5-10 videos of a takeover to frontend. The front end SDKs are expected to dynamically adjust viewports depending on the number of videos sent for the takeover(5-10) per pagination 3.2 Sponsored Post A sponsored post occupies only the designated in-feed ad slots within the paginated view (a placement-level configuration — e.g. 5 in-feed slots out of 10). It does not occupy the full view. Any in-feed slots not filled by a sponsored post fall back to programmatic ads. Sponsored posts are suppressed entirely when a takeover is active on that placement.

question: What is the significance of the Sponsored Takeover ad type on the Genuin platform, and how does it differ from Sponsored Posts in terms of ad placement and impact?
reference: The Sponsored Takeover ad type on the Genuin platform is significant because it converts the first 'n' slots of the video feed into a continuous, brand-sponsored experience, showcasing only the sponsor's video content instead of organic feed posts. This format is the highest-impact in-feed placement available, as it overrides all other in-feed ad types for its occupied slots, ensuring maximum visibility for the brand. In contrast, Sponsored Posts are individual in-feed cards that contain brand-sponsored video content but follow the standard slot frequency logic, appearing interleaved with organic content at calculated ad slot positions. Thus, while Sponsored Takeovers dominate the feed entirely, Sponsored Posts integrate with the regular content flow, making the former a more aggressive advertising strategy compared to the latter.

Ads are requested in advance of the break point, so content continues to play while the ad loads. The ad fires as soon as it is ready. Pre-roll: ad request sent at content start Mid-roll: ad request sent ~10–12 seconds before midpoint Post-roll: ad request sent ~10 seconds before content ends 4.3.2 Server-Side Timeout Each demand source has a configurable maximum response time (default 2,000 ms). This value is tunable per demand source in BCC. Experiments are recommended to find the ideal timeout — a lower timeout reduces latency but may increase unfilled breaks. 4.3.3 Skippability The player respects the skipOffset defined in the VAST creative. After the skip offset elapses, users can either tap the skip control or swipe past the ad. Ads beyond 15 seconds must be skippable per IAB guidelines. Shorter ads may be non-skippable. 4.3.4 Dynamic Cue Points Break positions are determined dynamically based on content video length — there are no fixed timestamps. This ensures appropriate ad placement across short-form content of varying durations. 4.4 In-Stream Ad Ops Recommendations Use 15–30 second creatives for best performance in short-form environments. Target ad response within 2–6 seconds for programmatic demand to reduce timeouts. Limit VAST wrapper depth to 1–2 layers to minimise latency. Configure server-side timeout per demand source — test at 2,000 ms and adjust based on fill rate and latency. One ad per request — podding is not supported. Vertical creatives (9:16) are strongly recommended for mobile-first placements.

question: What are the primary user experiences in Genuin that contribute to product and engineering integration, and how do they enhance user experiences in Community Media Networks?
reference: The primary user experiences in Genuin that contribute to product and engineering integration include the Product, Engineering & Developer Experience and the Brand & Business Experience. The Product, Engineering & Developer Experience focuses on embedding Genuin into existing web and app environments while maintaining performance and control. This experience is crucial for product managers and engineers as it enables seamless integration, context-aware personalization, and scalability. On the other hand, the Brand & Business Experience is designed for publishers and brands to operate their own Community Media Networks, allowing them to own distribution and audience relationships. Together, these experiences enhance user experiences by ensuring that community and video interactions are integrated effectively, leading to improved engagement, loyalty, and monetization outcomes within the Community Media Network.
